newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: Iran says spent $300 mln to halt drug traffic. [CORRECTED 08:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Iran says spent $300 mln to halt drug traffic. [CORRECTED 08:55 GMT]

text.p: Iran, a key drugs transit route to Europe, said it spent $300 million in 1996 to prevent smugglers from neighbouring Afghanistan and Pakistan using it for shipments.
"The amount of money spent on fortification at the eastern borders by the end 1996 has been $300 million," Mohammad Fallah of Iran's anti-drug committee said.

Fallah, addressing a four-day international conference on drug demand reduction that opened in Abu Dhabi on Sunday, said that included road works, observation posts and blocking passes used by traffickers.
But he said Iran's anti-drugs policy had not halted shipments of drugs through its territory due to lack of cooperation by regional states.
Traffickers use Iran as a route for drugs, mainly opium from which heroin is made, to reach Europe via Turkey from Afghanistan and Pakistan -- the so called "Golden Crescent".
Fallah said Iran had confiscated about 150 tonnes (330,690 pounds) (Corrects from 1.5 tonnes) of opium and 804 kg (1,770 pounds) of heroin in 1996.

Under Iranian law, possession of five kg (11 pounds) of opium and 30 grammes (just over one ounce) of heroin is punishable by death. More than 1,000 people have been executed since the law took effect in 1989.
